messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: NEW INCIDENT - streaming_latency_p99_surge - severity: P1
incident-bot: Trigger conditions: streaming p99 > 1.8s for 4m in eu-west-1, route=/v1/stream/generate, auto-paging: on

maria: paging @jamal @alice @eva @kevin — I'm taking command for initial triage. summary: users reporting timeouts, telemetry shows p99 spike and increased streaming stalls.

jamal: pulling graphs now. can someone confirm which nodes are serving heavy streaming load?

alice: quick inventory:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=model-server -o wide
model-server-2a  Running 1/1  node=gpu-ax-14 10.0.40.14
model-server-2b  Running 1/1  node=gpu-ax-14 10.0.40.15
model-server-7c  Running 1/1  node=gpu-bx-03 10.0.41.03
```

alice: ssh'd to gpu-ax-14: fans are ramping frequently, nvme temps normal, but nvidia-smi reports growing correctable ECC counters.

eva: model runtime reports many streaming sessions waiting on GPU response; KV prefetch latency jumps correlate with the p99. We see GRPC stalls in logs: "server-side deadline exceeded" for some streams.

maria: customer impact?

kevin: support: 5 distinct customer reports of timeouts in last 20m, two escalations opened (trial customers). Roughly 12% of streaming traffic experienced degraded UX. No broad 5xx spike.

jamal: plotting metrics (last 30m): requests/s steady ~480, p95 ~140ms, p99 max 2.4s, streaming-stall-events +380 above baseline, GPU ECC correctable delta on gpu-ax-14 = +700 in 30m.

jamal: likely hardware-level micro-pauses (ECC/thermal) on gpu-ax-14 causing transient stalls; streaming backend queues accumulate -> tail latency.

alice: dmesg snippet from gpu-ax-14: 
```
[12045.987654] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, pid=2048, GPU stall
[12046.012345] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: ECC: correctable error count incremented
[12046.500000] kernel: nvidia gpu reset requested
```

maria: immediate options: 1) cordon+drain gpu-ax-14, migrate streaming pods to gpu-bx-03 (lower load), 2) enable quantized fallback for streaming route to reduce GPU time per-token, 3) temporarily throttle per-connection streaming window to limit backlog.

jamal: we should cordon+drain to stop new sessions hitting the flaky node. Alice, can you start the node ops? I'll coordinate routes.

alice: running: `kubectl cordon gpu-ax-14 && kubectl drain gpu-ax-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — evictions starting, will allow graceful session handoff where possible.

incident-bot: Action recorded: node cordoned/drain initiated by alice at 2026-03-15T12:38:02Z

maria: eva, please flip the runtime route to quantized-variant-2 at 80% for 15m and monitor p99. keep 20% on original for validation.

eva: applying: `redwood-cli routes update --path /v1/stream/generate --split 80:quantized-variant-2,20:base-variant --duration 15m`

eva: also increasing KV cache eviction threshold to avoid unbounded growth during failover.

jamal: 6m after mitigations: p95 150ms, p99 360ms, streaming stalls back to baseline within 8m. customer reports reduced. Good sign.

kevin: support: notifying affected customers with status note and mitigations. no urgent escalations now.

maria: Alice — please open hardware case with vendor, attach dmesg and nvidia-smi logs. tag vendor-bot once issued.

alice: opened case with vendor: VG-CASE-2026-981, attaching logs. vendor-bot acknowledged. Node quarantined pending vendor instructions.

vendor-bot: Case VG-CASE-2026-981 received. Vendor requested full nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY + ECC logs and BIOS/system logs. ETA 24h for initial triage.

jamal: short post-incident actions:
- add alert for rapid ECC correctable delta (threshold: >100/min)
- add streaming backpressure limiter to runtime to cap per-connection queue length
- add KV cache growth rate metric + alert when growth > x MB/min
- evaluate adding a heartbeat watchdog to preempt long GPU stalls and fail fast to fallback variant

eva: I'll own KV cache metric + runtime flag for per-connection queue cap (PR after incident).

alice: hardware followup: RMA if vendor confirms card-level fault; revisit node-level cooling profile if thermal cycling persists.

maria: assigning owners: jamal (SRE/incident writeup), eva (runtime mitigations), alice (hardware/vendor followup), kevin (customer comms).

maria: keeping thread open until vendor next update and p99 stable for 30m. If any customer escalations, escalate to incident commander.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated — monitoring for stability :white_check_mark:

kevin: sent follow-up message to impacted orgs and logged customer replies. no additional reports in last 12m.

jamal: creating short-lived dashboard to track ECC deltas, streaming-stall-events, p99 for eu-west-1, and routing-split percentages.

maria: thanks team. when we close, we will produce a postmortem covering root cause, detection gaps, and the mitigation timeline. keep logs and ingress traces attached to the incident ticket.

alice: vendor updated: preliminary triage suggests intermittent L1 cache ECC bursts; vendor advises testing with different driver/firmware before RMA. scheduling windows.

maria: noted. continue monitoring. Close ticket after 30m stable and vendor confirms next steps.

incident-bot: INCIDENT ACTION: mitigations recorded, owners assigned, follow-ups created.
